1.title: Made in God’s Image
1.studyConnection: Genesis opens with God bringing life into being and giving human beings a distinct place within creation.
1.verseContext: The verse names both male and female as people God made in his image.

phrases.quote: So God created man in his own image; he created him in the image of God;
phrases.question: What changes when I remember that my worth begins with how God made me?
phrases.prayer: Creator, help me receive the worth you’ve given me.

phrases.quote: he created them male and female.
phrases.question: Who is easy for me to overlook, and how might I see them differently as someone God made in his image?
phrases.prayer: God, help me see and honor the person in front of me.

8.title: Abram Believed the Lord
8.studyConnection: Abram tells God he still has no child. God takes him outside and promises offspring as numerous as the stars.
8.verseContext: Abram trusts the Lord’s promise while the circumstances he just described still stand.

phrases.quote: Abram believed the Lord,
phrases.question: What is hard to trust about God while my circumstances stay the same?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me trust you in what I can’t yet see.

phrases.quote: and he credited it to him as righteousness.
phrases.question: Where do I feel that I have to prove myself before I can trust God to receive me?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me lean on you where I’m trying to prove myself.

15.title: God Himself Will Provide
15.studyConnection: Isaac asks Abraham where the lamb is. Abraham answers before either of them sees the ram God provides.
15.verseContext: These are Abraham’s words to Isaac during a particular test. God stops Abraham and provides a ram in Isaac’s place.

phrases.quote: Abraham answered, “God himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.”
phrases.question: Where is it hard to trust God when I can’t see how he will provide?
phrases.prayer: God, help me trust you while I wait.

phrases.quote: Then the two of them walked on together.
phrases.question: What step can I take in trust while I still have unanswered questions?
phrases.prayer: Lord, give me enough trust for the next step.

22.title: The Lord Is in This Place
22.studyConnection: Jacob is traveling away from home when God meets him in a dream and promises to be with him wherever he goes.
22.verseContext: Jacob speaks these words after waking. He recognizes God’s presence in a place where he had simply stopped for the night.

phrases.quote: Surely the Lord is in this place,
phrases.question: What ordinary place in my day could I receive as a place to pay attention to God?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me notice your presence where I already am.

phrases.quote: and I did not know it.
phrases.question: When have I recognized God’s care only after looking back?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me see what I missed and thank you for it.

29.title: Remembering Your Kindness
29.studyConnection: Jacob hears that Esau is approaching with four hundred men. Before they meet, Jacob prays and remembers what God has already done.
29.verseContext: Jacob remembers God’s kindness as part of a prayer that also names his real fear of Esau.

phrases.quote: I am unworthy of all the kindness and faithfulness
phrases.question: What kindness have I come to take for granted?
phrases.prayer: God, help me receive your kindness again with gratitude.

phrases.quote: you have shown your servant.
phrases.question: What past sign of God’s faithfulness can I remember as I bring him a fear today?
phrases.prayer: Lord, thank you for how you’ve cared for me. Hear what I’m afraid of now.

36.title: With Joseph in Prison
36.studyConnection: Joseph is imprisoned after being falsely accused. The story names God’s presence with him while he is still there.
36.verseContext: God’s kindness in this scene includes favor with the prison warden. Joseph’s circumstances have yet to change.

phrases.quote: But the Lord was with Joseph and extended kindness to him.
phrases.question: Where is it hardest for me to believe God is with me while the situation is still unresolved?
phrases.prayer: Lord, meet me in what hasn’t changed.

phrases.quote: He granted him favor with the prison warden.
phrases.question: What ordinary act of kindness might I have missed because I was looking for a bigger change?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me recognize and receive the kindness you’re giving me today.

43.title: The Survival of Many
43.studyConnection: After Jacob dies, Joseph’s brothers fear that Joseph will take revenge. Joseph names the harm they intended, explains what God brought about, and promises to provide for them.
43.verseContext: Joseph is looking back on a specific wrong and the lives that were preserved through what followed.

phrases.quote: You planned evil against me;
phrases.question: What wrong do I need to name honestly before God?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me tell the truth about what hurt.

phrases.quote: God planned it for good to bring about the present result—the survival of many people.
phrases.question: Is there any good I can name today without pretending the harm was good?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me notice the good you’ve brought and trust you where I still have questions.

50.title: Come to Me
50.studyConnection: Jesus invites the weary to come to him. In the next verses he asks them to take his yoke and learn from him because he is gentle and humble.
50.verseContext: Jesus’ promise of rest is an invitation to come to him and learn his way.

phrases.quote: Come to me, all of you who are weary and burdened,
phrases.question: What burden am I carrying as though I have to carry it alone?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, I’m weary. Help me come to you with what I’m carrying.

phrases.quote: and I will give you rest.
phrases.question: What makes it hard to receive the rest Jesus offers?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, teach me to receive your rest and learn from you.

57.title: Here to Serve
57.studyConnection: When the disciples argue over places of honor, Jesus contrasts the way rulers exercise power with how his followers are to serve.
57.verseContext: Jesus points to his own service, which culminates in giving his life for many.

phrases.quote: just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve,
phrases.question: Where do I expect to be noticed when I could quietly serve someone?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me use what I have to serve.

phrases.quote: and to give his life as a ransom for many.
phrases.question: What changes about how I serve when I remember what Jesus has already given for me?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, thank you for giving your life. Let your generosity shape mine.

64.title: With You Always
64.studyConnection: The risen Jesus sends his disciples to make disciples of all nations and closes with a promise of his presence.
64.verseContext: Jesus promises his presence as he sends his disciples out to teach and make disciples.

phrases.quote: And remember, I am with you always,
phrases.question: Where do I hesitate to share what Jesus has taught me because I feel alone?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me remember you are with me as I go.

phrases.quote: to the end of the age.
phrases.question: What changes when I take seriously how long Jesus promises to be with his people?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me trust that your presence outlasts what I’m facing.

71.title: I Will Be With You
71.studyConnection: God hears Israel’s cries and sends Moses to Pharaoh. Moses asks who he is to take on such a task.
71.verseContext: God answers Moses’ question about his own ability with a promise of God’s presence.

phrases.quote: I will certainly be with you,
phrases.question: Where am I focused on whether I’m enough when I could pay attention to who is with me?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me trust your presence where I feel inadequate.

78.title: At the Sea
78.studyConnection: Israel is trapped between Pharaoh’s army and the sea. Moses tells the people to be quiet, and God then tells them to move forward.
78.verseContext: Moses speaks to Israel at the sea. God’s rescue comes as the people follow his direction to move forward.

phrases.quote: The Lord will fight for you,
phrases.question: What situation have I taken to mean that I must fix everything myself?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me entrust to you what I can’t fix.

phrases.quote: and you must be quiet.
phrases.question: What would help me quiet my panic enough to listen for the next faithful step?
phrases.prayer: Lord, quiet my fear and help me listen.

85.title: Brought to Myself
85.studyConnection: At Sinai, before he sets out the terms of the covenant, God reminds Israel that he has already rescued them.
85.verseContext: God describes the exodus as bringing Israel to himself.

phrases.quote: You have seen what I did to the Egyptians
phrases.question: What has God already done that I tend to forget when I face a new demand?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me remember your care before I rush into what’s next.

phrases.quote: and how I carried you on eagles’ wings and brought you to myself.
phrases.question: Where have I noticed God’s care drawing me closer to him?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me see how you have carried me and respond by drawing near.

92.title: Dwell Among Them
92.studyConnection: God asks for offerings from willing hearts and gives Moses directions for building the sanctuary.
92.verseContext: God tells Moses why Israel is to build the sanctuary: he intends to dwell among them.

phrases.quote: They are to make a sanctuary for me
phrases.question: Where could I make room in my day to pay attention to God?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me make room for you with a willing heart.

phrases.quote: so that I may dwell among them.
phrases.question: What changes when I remember that God desires to be among his people?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me welcome your presence in the ordinary places of my life.

99.title: Compassionate and Gracious
99.studyConnection: After Israel makes the golden calf, the Lord meets Moses and reveals his character as the covenant is renewed.
99.verseContext: God describes his compassion, patience, and faithful love in the wake of Israel’s serious wrongdoing.

phrases.quote: The Lord—the Lord is a compassionate and gracious God,
phrases.question: What am I afraid to tell God about myself, even after hearing how he describes himself?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me bring this honestly to you and trust your compassion.

phrases.quote: slow to anger and abounding in faithful love and truth,
phrases.question: Where would remembering God’s patience help me respond more patiently to someone else?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me show the patience I’ve received from you.

106.title: The Wind Ceased
106.studyConnection: The disciples wake Jesus in a storm and ask whether he cares. After he calms the sea, they ask who he is.
106.verseContext: Jesus speaks to an actual storm. The disciples are left wondering who has authority even over the wind and sea.

phrases.quote: He got up, rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Silence! Be still!”
phrases.question: When I feel overlooked in trouble, what would I say to Jesus if I were as honest as the disciples?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me tell you what frightens me.

phrases.quote: The wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
phrases.question: What do I learn about Jesus from the disciples’ surprise that the wind and sea obey him?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me trust who you are when I can’t yet see what will happen.

113.title: Help My Unbelief
113.studyConnection: A father asks Jesus to help his son after the disciples could not. He brings faith and doubt to Jesus in the same breath.

phrases.quote: I do believe;
phrases.question: What do I believe about Jesus that I could say aloud today?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me name what I believe about you.

phrases.quote: help my unbelief!
phrases.question: What am I still afraid to trust you with?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, meet me where trusting you is hard.

120.title: Love God With All You Are
120.studyConnection: Asked which command comes first, Jesus calls for wholehearted love for God and immediately joins it to love for one’s neighbor.

phrases.quote: Love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul,
phrases.question: What has most of my affection and attention right now?
phrases.prayer: Lord, draw my heart toward you.

phrases.quote: with all your mind, and with all your strength.
phrases.question: How could I give God my attention and effort in a task I already have today?
phrases.prayer: Lord, let the way I think and work show my love for you.

127.title: The Glory of the Lord
127.studyConnection: At the start of Aaron’s priestly service, Moses tells Israel what God commanded. After the offerings, God’s glory appears to the gathered people.

phrases.quote: This is what the Lord commanded you to do,
phrases.question: What direction from God have I heard clearly but left for later?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me respond to what you’ve already shown me.

phrases.quote: that the glory of the Lord may appear to you.
phrases.question: Where do I rush through worship without attending to the God I’ve come to worship?
phrases.prayer: Lord, turn my attention toward you.

134.title: Clean Before the Lord
134.studyConnection: On the Day of Atonement, the priest makes atonement to cleanse Israel from its sins before God.

phrases.quote: Atonement will be made for you on this day to cleanse you,
phrases.question: What wrong am I tempted to cover up when I could bring it honestly to God?
phrases.prayer: Lord, give me courage to confess what I’ve hidden.

phrases.quote: and you will be clean from all your sins before the Lord.
phrases.question: What keeps me from receiving forgiveness after I’ve confessed?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me trust your mercy more than my shame.

141.title: Beyond the Grudge
141.studyConnection: God gives Israel concrete instructions for dealing fairly with neighbors, addressing wrong, and refusing revenge.

phrases.quote: Do not take revenge or bear a grudge against members of your community,
phrases.question: When I replay a wrong, what am I hoping the other person will have to pay?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me bring my anger to you and let go of revenge.

phrases.quote: but love your neighbor as yourself; I am the Lord.
phrases.question: What is one way I could seek my neighbor’s good without ignoring the harm?
phrases.prayer: Lord, show me how to love wisely in this relationship.

148.title: I Will Walk Among You
148.studyConnection: As part of his covenant blessings, God promises Israel his presence and reminds them that he brought them out of slavery.

phrases.quote: I will walk among you and be your God,
phrases.question: What ordinary part of my day could I spend more aware of God’s presence?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me walk through today with you.

phrases.quote: and you will be my people.
phrases.question: Where do I need to remember that belonging to God also means belonging with others?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me make room for your people in my life.

155.title: Ask, Seek, Knock
155.studyConnection: After teaching his disciples to pray, Jesus encourages them to keep asking. He points to the Father’s goodness and his gift of the Holy Spirit.

phrases.quote: So I say to you, ask, and it will be given to you.
phrases.question: What have I held back from asking the Father for?
phrases.prayer: Father, help me ask you honestly for what I need.

phrases.quote: Seek, and you will find.
phrases.question: What would it look like to seek God himself while I wait for an answer?
phrases.prayer: Father, help me keep looking for you in this.

phrases.quote: Knock, and the door will be opened to you.
phrases.question: What prayer have I let go because I grew tired of waiting?
phrases.prayer: Father, help me return to you with that prayer.

162.title: To Seek and to Save
162.studyConnection: Jesus chooses to stay with Zacchaeus despite the crowd’s objections. He explains the visit by naming why he came.

phrases.quote: For the Son of Man has come
phrases.question: What does Jesus choosing to approach Zacchaeus show me about how he comes near?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me welcome you into my ordinary life.

phrases.quote: to seek and to save the lost.
phrases.question: Who do I tend to write off that Jesus’ mission asks me to see differently?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me see that person with mercy.

169.title: Not My Will
169.studyConnection: On the Mount of Olives before his arrest, Jesus tells the Father what he wants and entrusts himself to the Father’s will. His prayer holds honesty and surrender together.

phrases.quote: Father, if you are willing, take this cup away from me—
phrases.question: What do I want God to change that I’ve been reluctant to say plainly?
phrases.prayer: Father, help me tell you honestly what I want.

phrases.quote: nevertheless, not my will, but yours, be done.
phrases.question: Where is it hardest to remain open to the Father’s will after I’ve asked for what I want?
phrases.prayer: Father, help me trust you with what happens next.

176.title: Give You Peace
176.studyConnection: God gives Aaron and his sons words to bless Israel. The blessing ends by asking the Lord to look on his people with favor and give them peace.

phrases.quote: may the Lord look with favor on you
phrases.question: What makes it hard to receive God’s kindness without first trying to earn it?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me receive your kindness with open hands.

phrases.quote: and give you peace.
phrases.question: What unsettled part of my day can I bring to God as I ask for peace?
phrases.prayer: Lord, give me your peace in what feels unsettled today.

183.title: The Lord Is With Us
183.studyConnection: Israel wants to turn back after hearing the scouts’ report. Joshua and Caleb urge the people to trust the Lord in the face of what they saw.

phrases.quote: and the Lord is with us.
phrases.question: What part of a hard situation am I picturing as though God were absent?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me remember your presence when the difficulty fills my view.

phrases.quote: Don’t be afraid of them!
phrases.question: What is one faithful step fear is making hard to take?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me take the next faithful step even while I’m afraid.

190.title: Does He Promise and Not Fulfill?
190.studyConnection: Balak wants Balaam to curse Israel. Balaam explains that he cannot reverse the blessing God has given.

phrases.quote: Does he speak and not act,
phrases.question: Where am I treating God’s words as less reliable than someone else’s pressure or opinion?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me give your words more weight than the voices pressing on me.

phrases.quote: or promise and not fulfill?
phrases.question: What promise in Scripture can I return to when I feel unsure of God’s faithfulness?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me remember what you have actually promised and trust you to keep it.

197.title: A Shepherd for the People
197.studyConnection: As Moses learns that he will not lead Israel into the land, he asks God to appoint someone to care for the people. God names Joshua.

phrases.quote: who will go out before them and come back in before them,
phrases.question: What responsibility calls for me to walk alongside people today?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me stay present with the people you’ve entrusted to me.

phrases.quote: so that the Lord’s community won’t be like sheep without a shepherd.
phrases.question: Who might feel left to figure things out alone right now?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me notice who needs care and respond with humility.

204.title: The Word Among Us
204.studyConnection: John opens his Gospel by naming the Word who was with God and was God. He then says that this Word became flesh and lived among us.

phrases.quote: The Word became flesh
phrases.question: What does Jesus taking on human life show me about God’s willingness to come near?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, thank you for coming close enough to share our human life.

phrases.quote: and dwelt among us.
phrases.question: Where do I still imagine that ordinary life is beneath God’s attention?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me welcome you into what feels ordinary today.

211.title: Hear His Voice
211.studyConnection: Jesus describes his sheep as hearing him, being known by him, and following him. The next verses speak of the life and security he gives them.

phrases.quote: My sheep hear my voice, I know them,
phrases.question: What changes about listening to Jesus when I remember that he already knows me?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me listen to you without hiding who I am.

phrases.quote: and they follow me.
phrases.question: What is one thing Jesus has already taught me that I could put into practice today?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me follow what I’ve heard from you.

218.title: Remain in My Love
218.studyConnection: Speaking to his disciples on the night before his death, Jesus connects remaining in him with receiving his love and keeping his commands.

phrases.quote: As the Father has loved me, I have also loved you.
phrases.question: What do I find hardest to believe about the love Jesus says he has for his disciples?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me receive the love you say is yours to give.

phrases.quote: Remain in my love.
phrases.question: What would it look like to obey Jesus today as someone who is already loved?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me stay close to you and let your love shape how I obey.

225.title: And Yet Believe
225.studyConnection: The risen Jesus meets Thomas in his doubt. John then explains that he recorded these signs so others might believe.

phrases.quote: Blessed are those who have not seen
phrases.question: What do I wish I could see for myself before I trust Jesus?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me bring that desire to you honestly.

phrases.quote: and yet believe.
phrases.question: What in John’s account gives me reason to trust the risen Jesus today?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me attend to what your witnesses saw and told us.

232.title: More Than Bread
232.studyConnection: Moses reminds Israel that hunger and manna in the wilderness taught them to depend on what God says.

phrases.quote: man does not live on bread alone
phrases.question: What immediate need tends to crowd out my attention to God?
phrases.prayer: Lord, you know my needs. Help me remember all I depend on you for.

phrases.quote: but on every word that comes from the mouth of the Lord.
phrases.question: What word from God could I carry into the part of today that feels most demanding?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me listen and live by what you say.

239.title: An Open Hand
239.studyConnection: Moses tells Israel to lend freely to a neighbor in need even when the year for canceling debts is close.

phrases.quote: Instead, you are to open your hand to him
phrases.question: What makes my first instinct to hold back when someone needs help?
phrases.prayer: Lord, open my hands where I’m tempted to close them.

phrases.quote: and freely loan him enough for whatever need he has.
phrases.question: Do I know what the person actually needs, or have I assumed I know?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me listen and give in a way that meets a real need.

246.title: Remember Where You Came From
246.studyConnection: Israel’s rescue from slavery is the reason Moses gives for protecting people who can easily be denied justice.

phrases.quote: Remember that you were a slave in Egypt,
phrases.question: When has needing someone else’s help taught me how to see people more clearly?
phrases.prayer: Lord, keep me from forgetting what it felt like to need help.

phrases.quote: and the Lord your God redeemed you from there.
phrases.question: How could remembering God’s mercy change the way I treat someone with less power than I have?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me let the mercy I’ve received shape how I use what I have.

253.title: He Will Go Before You
253.studyConnection: As Joshua prepares to lead Israel into the land, Moses tells him that the Lord will go ahead of him and stay with him.

phrases.quote: The Lord is the one who will go before you.
phrases.question: What responsibility am I picturing as though I’ll be the first one there?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me trust you as I step into what I can’t yet see.

phrases.quote: He will be with you; he will not leave you or abandon you.
phrases.question: Where do I need to remember God’s presence more than I need certainty about the outcome?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me remember that I don’t have to walk through this alone.

260.title: Boldness to Speak
260.studyConnection: After Peter and John are threatened, the believers pray together. They bring the threats to God and ask for courage to keep speaking.

phrases.quote: And now, Lord, consider their threats,
phrases.question: What pressure could I name plainly to God today?
phrases.prayer: Lord, you see what I’m up against. Help me bring it to you.

phrases.quote: and grant that your servants may speak your word with all boldness,
phrases.question: What could I say about Jesus with courage and kindness where I’m tempted to stay silent?
phrases.prayer: Lord, give me courage to speak your word faithfully.

267.title: God Shows No Favoritism
267.studyConnection: Peter enters the Gentile Cornelius’s home and recognizes that God has taught him to see people differently. He goes on to proclaim peace through Jesus.

phrases.quote: Now I truly understand that God doesn’t show favoritism,
phrases.question: Whom do I tend to assume is less open to God because of their background?
phrases.prayer: Lord, show me where my assumptions keep me from seeing people as you do.

phrases.quote: but in every nation the person who fears him and does what is right is acceptable to him.
phrases.question: Whose faithfulness might I notice if I looked beyond what feels familiar to me?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me recognize where you’re at work beyond the people I know best.

274.title: He Is Not Far
274.studyConnection: In Athens, Paul speaks to people worshiping at many altars. He points them to the Creator who gives life and calls people to seek him.

phrases.quote: that they might seek God, and perhaps they might reach out and find him,
phrases.question: What would seeking God look like in the middle of an ordinary day?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me turn my attention to you in what I’m already doing.

phrases.quote: though he is not far from each one of us.
phrases.question: Where do I assume God is far away when I could turn toward him now?
phrases.prayer: God, help me attend to your nearness right here.

385.title: Make Room for Someone Else’s Joy
385.studyConnection: In 2 Samuel 1, David grieves for Saul and Jonathan and honors them publicly. Saul had made David’s life harder, yet David could still speak honestly about what was worth honoring in him.

phrases.quote: Rejoice with those who rejoice
phrases.question: When someone else gets something I’ve been hoping for, what would it look like to enjoy their good news with them?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me enjoy the good you give others. Give me something honest and generous to say.

phrases.quote: weep with those who weep.
phrases.question: Whose grief do I hurry past because I don’t know what to say?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me slow down and be present with someone who’s hurting.

385.verseContext: Paul describes sincere love as sharing in one another’s joy and grief.

392.title: Make Room at the Table
392.studyConnection: In 2 Samuel 9, David gives Mephibosheth a place at his table. In Romans 15, Paul asks believers to welcome one another even when their convictions and practices differ, grounding that welcome in how Christ received them.

phrases.quote: Therefore welcome one another,
phrases.question: Who could I make more room for, even when our convictions differ?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, thank you for welcoming me. Help me make room for others as you made room for me.

phrases.quote: just as Christ also welcomed you, to the glory of God.
phrases.question: What about the way Christ welcomed me could shape how I receive others?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, thank you for welcoming me. Teach me to welcome others as you did.

392.verseContext: Paul urges believers with different convictions to welcome one another as Christ welcomed them.

399.title: Put Down What You’re Carrying
399.studyConnection: In 2 Samuel 15, David sends the ark back to Jerusalem and leaves the outcome with God. Peter gives us a reason we can entrust our own worries to God. He cares for us.

phrases.quote: casting all your cares on him
phrases.question: What care am I struggling to entrust to God, and what does Peter give me reason to believe about him?
phrases.prayer: Father, help me trust your care enough to put this worry in your hands.

phrases.quote: because he cares about you.
phrases.question: Which care is hardest to believe God notices?
phrases.prayer: Father, help me trust that you care about this.

399.verseContext: Peter calls believers to humble themselves under God’s mighty hand by entrusting their cares to him.

406.title: What I’m Glad to Talk About
406.studyConnection: In 1 Corinthians 1, Paul points a divided church back to what God has given them in Christ. His closing line gives us something to sit with when we feel the urge to make much of ourselves.

phrases.quote: Let the one who boasts,
phrases.question: Whose praise matters most when I tell a story about myself?
phrases.prayer: Lord, show me what I most want people to admire.

phrases.quote: boast in the Lord.
phrases.question: What good could I give God credit for today?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me speak gladly about what you’ve done.

406.verseContext: Paul points the church to what God has given them in Christ, including wisdom, righteousness, sanctification, and redemption.

413.title: A Place in the Body
413.studyConnection: In 1 Corinthians 6–12, Paul connects belonging to Christ with how believers live together. In chapter 12, even the members who seem weaker are indispensable.
413.verseContext: Paul tells the church that they belong to Christ together, each as a member of his body.

phrases.quote: Now you are the body of Christ,
phrases.question: Where am I trying to follow Jesus alone?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me let your people walk with me.

phrases.quote: and individual members of it.
phrases.question: What makes me doubt that I have a place in Christ’s body?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me receive the place you’ve given me.

420.title: The Victory God Gives
420.studyConnection: In 1 Corinthians 15, Paul looks ahead to the resurrection of the dead and ends by thanking God for the victory he gives through Jesus.
420.verseContext: Paul thanks God because Jesus’ resurrection gives believers hope of victory over death.

phrases.quote: But thanks be to God,
phrases.question: What can I thank God for about Jesus even while I grieve?
phrases.prayer: Father, thank you for raising Jesus.

phrases.quote: who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ!
phrases.question: What fear about death can I entrust to the risen Jesus?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me trust you with what I fear about dying.

427.title: Be With Us
427.studyConnection: At the temple dedication in 1 Kings 8, Solomon remembers how God kept his promises to Israel and asks God to stay with his people.
427.verseContext: In the next verse, Solomon asks that God’s presence turn Israel’s heart toward him and help them walk in his ways.

phrases.quote: May the Lord our God be with us as he was with our ancestors.
phrases.question: Where do I need God’s nearness to help me obey?
phrases.prayer: Lord, be with us as you were with your people before.

phrases.quote: May he not abandon us or leave us
phrases.question: When God feels far away, what am I tempted to assume about him?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me keep talking to you when you feel far away.

434.title: An Undivided Heart
434.studyConnection: In 1 Kings 18, Elijah asks Israel how long they’ll waver between the Lord and Baal. Psalm 86 gives us words for bringing our own divided loyalties to God.
434.verseContext: The psalmist asks God to teach him how to live and to give him an undivided mind.

phrases.quote: Teach me your way, Lord,
phrases.question: Where have I already made up my mind while still asking God to guide me?
phrases.prayer: Lord, make me willing to hear you.

phrases.quote: and I will live by your truth.
phrases.question: What truth about God could change how I respond today?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me live by what you show me.

phrases.quote: Give me an undivided mind to fear your name.
phrases.question: Whose approval carries the most weight when I’m deciding whether to obey God?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me care most about what honors you.

441.title: The God of All Comfort
441.verseContext: Paul opens his letter by blessing God for the comfort he gives in suffering, which enables us to comfort others.

phrases.quote: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,
phrases.question: What does it mean to me that the Father Jesus knows is the God I can turn to?
phrases.prayer: Father of Jesus, help me turn toward you in my need.

phrases.quote: the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort.
phrases.question: What hurts that I could bring to the Father for comfort?
phrases.prayer: Father, meet me in what hurts and help me receive your comfort.

448.title: Treasure in Clay Jars
448.verseContext: Paul calls the knowledge of God’s glory in Jesus a treasure. He and his fellow workers are like fragile jars that show where the power comes from.

phrases.quote: Now we have this treasure in clay jars,
phrases.question: Can I be honest about my limits while still valuing what God has entrusted to me?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me be honest about my limits.

phrases.quote: so that this extraordinary power may be from God and not from us.
phrases.question: Where am I tempted to act as if the strength I need has to come from me?
phrases.prayer: God, let your power be seen where my strength runs out.

455.title: Grace for What Remains
455.verseContext: After Paul asks three times for his thorn to be taken away, Jesus answers with these words. Paul learns to welcome Christ’s power in his weakness.

phrases.quote: My grace is sufficient for you,
phrases.question: What have I asked Jesus to take away, and where do I still need his grace as I wait?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, you know what I wish would change. Give me the grace I need to face it with you today.

phrases.quote: for my power is perfected in weakness.
phrases.question: Where am I afraid that my weakness makes me useless to Christ?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, let your power meet me in the weakness I want to hide.

462.title: When All I Can See Is the Threat
462.verseContext: Elisha says this to his servant when an army surrounds the city. He then asks God to open the servant’s eyes.

phrases.quote: Elisha said, “Don’t be afraid,
phrases.question: What fear takes up most of my attention right now?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me name my fear honestly before you.

phrases.quote: for those who are with us outnumber those who are with them.”
phrases.question: What can I remember about God when all I can see is what threatens me?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me trust you with what I can’t see.

469.title: Spread It Out Before the Lord
469.verseContext: When Assyria threatens Jerusalem, Hezekiah brings the letter to the temple and lays the threat before God in prayer.

phrases.quote: Hezekiah took the letter from the messengers’ hands, read it,
phrases.question: What news or conversation have I been replaying that I could lay before God in prayer?
phrases.prayer: Lord, you know what I’m afraid will happen. Help me tell you plainly and entrust it to you.

phrases.quote: then went up to the Lord’s temple, and spread it out before the Lord.
phrases.question: What would it sound like to lay my specific fear before God?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me tell you plainly what I’m afraid will happen.

476.title: When the Word Gets Through
476.verseContext: When Josiah hears the book of the law, he tears his clothes in grief because Judah has disregarded what God commanded.

phrases.quote: When the king heard the words of the book of the law,
phrases.question: When Scripture shows me something I’ve been excusing, what helps me listen honestly?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me take your words seriously. Give me the humility to turn when you show me where I’ve gone wrong.

phrases.quote: he tore his clothes.
phrases.question: What might an honest response look like when Scripture shows me I’ve gone wrong?
phrases.prayer: Lord, give me the humility to turn when your word reaches me.

483.title: No Condemnation in Christ
483.verseContext: After asking who will rescue him, Paul points to Jesus Christ and announces that those in Christ are free from condemnation.

phrases.quote: Therefore, there is now no condemnation
phrases.question: What failure makes me want to hide from God?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me confess what I’ve done.

phrases.quote: for those in Christ Jesus,
phrases.question: What changes when I remember that I belong to Christ?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me come to you honestly because I belong to you.

490.title: Hope, Patience, and Prayer
490.verseContext: Paul describes how sincere love takes shape in the church, including how believers hold on to hope and keep praying through hardship.

phrases.quote: Rejoice in hope;
phrases.question: What reason for hope can I remember in the middle of this hardship?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me hold on to the hope you give today.

phrases.quote: be patient in affliction;
phrases.question: What hardship is testing my patience right now?
phrases.prayer: Lord, give me patience for what I have to face today.

phrases.quote: be persistent in prayer.
phrases.question: What have I grown tired of bringing to God?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me keep talking to you about this.

497.title: Learn to Do What Is Good
497.studyConnection: God tells Judah through Isaiah that their worship rings hollow while they tolerate injustice.
497.verseContext: Judah is still bringing offerings. God calls them to turn from wrongdoing and defend people who are easily overlooked.

phrases.quote: Learn to do what is good. Pursue justice. Correct the oppressor.
phrases.question: Whose need have I learned to walk past, even while I’m doing things I think of as worship?
phrases.prayer: Lord, show me who I’ve overlooked and teach me what doing good looks like for them.

phrases.quote: Defend the rights of the fatherless. Plead the widow’s cause.
phrases.question: Whose concern could I help someone take seriously?
phrases.prayer: Lord, give me courage to speak up for someone easily overlooked.

504.title: The Springs of Salvation
504.studyConnection: After Isaiah’s vision of the Lord gathering his scattered people, chapter 12 gives them a song of thanks.
504.verseContext: The song pictures God’s people drawing water with joy because he has become their salvation.

phrases.quote: You will joyfully draw water
phrases.question: What would it look like to receive God’s help with joy today?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me notice what you give with joy.

phrases.quote: from the springs of salvation,
phrases.question: What has God done to rescue or sustain me that I can thank him for?
phrases.prayer: Lord, thank you for the ways you’ve sustained me.

511.title: Eyes on Our Maker
511.studyConnection: In the oracle concerning Damascus, Isaiah also describes Israel’s strength fading and people turning back to their Maker.
511.verseContext: Isaiah sets looking to the Holy One of Israel alongside turning away from altars and idols people made themselves.

phrases.quote: On that day people will look to their Maker
phrases.question: What have I built, bought, or arranged that I’m counting on to give me the security I want from God?
phrases.prayer: Maker, turn my eyes back to you. Help me trust you with what my own hands can’t secure.

phrases.quote: and will turn their eyes to the Holy One of Israel.
phrases.question: What tends to take my attention back off God?
phrases.prayer: Holy One, turn my eyes back to you today.

518.title: A Mind That Depends on You
518.studyConnection: Amid Isaiah’s pictures of upheaval and deliverance, chapter 26 gives Judah a song about the security God provides.
518.verseContext: Judah’s song grounds peace in depending on the Lord, whom the next verse calls an everlasting rock.

phrases.quote: You will keep the mind that is dependent on you in perfect peace,
phrases.question: When my thoughts circle back to what I can’t control, what would it look like to depend on God in that moment?
phrases.prayer: Lord, when my mind goes back to the same worry, help me bring it back to you.

phrases.quote: for it is trusting in you.
phrases.question: What am I counting on to give me peace in this situation?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me depend on you when my thoughts circle back.

525.title: Returning and Resting
525.studyConnection: Judah was seeking Egypt’s protection. God called them to return and rest in him, and the people chose to flee on horses.
525.verseContext: Carry God’s whole reply to Judah, including the people’s unwillingness to trust him.

phrases.quote: You will be delivered by returning and resting;
phrases.question: When I feel pressed to act, what makes it hardest to slow down and listen to God?
phrases.prayer: Lord, show me where I’m running ahead of you. Help me return and trust you.

phrases.quote: your strength will lie in quiet confidence.
phrases.question: Where do I confuse urgency with faithfulness?
phrases.prayer: Lord, give me quiet confidence in you.

phrases.quote: But you are not willing.
phrases.question: What have I been unwilling to entrust to God?
phrases.prayer: Lord, show me where I’m resisting you and help me return.

532.title: Strength for the Faint
532.studyConnection: Isaiah answers Israel’s complaint that God has overlooked their troubles. The Creator never grows weary and gives strength to people who do.
532.verseContext: Israel feels unseen. Isaiah points them to the Lord’s strength for people who have run out of their own.

phrases.quote: He gives strength to the faint
phrases.question: Where have I been treating exhaustion as something I have to hide instead of something I can bring to God?
phrases.prayer: Lord, you see how tired I am. Give me strength for what’s in front of me today.

phrases.quote: and strengthens the powerless.
phrases.question: Where am I reluctant to admit how little strength I have?
phrases.prayer: Lord, give me strength where I have none to spare.

539.title: Still Before His Eyes
539.studyConnection: Zion says the Lord has forgotten her. God answers with the image of a mother and child, then pictures Zion’s walls continually before him.
539.verseContext: God is speaking to Zion, answering her fear that he has forgotten her and her ruined city.

phrases.quote: Look, I have inscribed you on the palms of my hands;
phrases.question: When I’m waiting for something broken to be restored, what makes me feel forgotten by God?
phrases.prayer: Lord, you see what’s still broken. Help me trust that it hasn’t slipped from your sight.

phrases.quote: your walls are continually before me.
phrases.question: What still looks broken that I struggle to believe God sees?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me trust that what’s broken hasn’t slipped from your sight.

546.title: Call While He Is Near
546.studyConnection: Isaiah invites the thirsty to come freely. The call to seek the Lord leads into an invitation to turn from evil and receive his generous forgiveness.
546.verseContext: The next verse tells those who return what they can expect from God: compassion and abundant forgiveness.

phrases.quote: Seek the Lord while he may be found;
phrases.question: What have I put off bringing to God because I’m unsure how he’ll receive me?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me turn toward you today. Thank you for meeting those who return with compassion.

phrases.quote: call to him while he is near.
phrases.question: What could I say to God right now if I believed he was near?
phrases.prayer: Lord, you are near. Help me speak to you honestly.

553.title: The Work of Your Hands
553.studyConnection: After remembering God’s mercy, the people confess their sin and ask him to look on their ruined city and sanctuary.
553.verseContext: In a prayer of confession and distress, the people still call God their Father and place themselves in his hands as clay.

phrases.quote: Yet Lord, you are our Father;
phrases.question: What is hard for me to believe about God as Father?
phrases.prayer: Father, help me trust that you know and care for me.

phrases.quote: we are the clay, and you are our potter;
phrases.question: Where am I resisting the way God may be shaping me?
phrases.prayer: Father, help me yield to your hands.

phrases.quote: we all are the work of your hands.
phrases.question: What changes when I see the person beside me as God’s handiwork too?
phrases.prayer: Father, help me receive others as people you made.

560.title: As God Forgave You
560.studyConnection: Paul gets specific about life in the church. He names the speech and anger that tear people down and calls believers to kindness and forgiveness.
560.verseContext: Paul grounds the call to forgive in what God has already done for believers in Christ.

phrases.quote: And be kind and compassionate to one another, forgiving one another,
phrases.question: When I replay a wrong someone did to me, how does remembering Christ’s forgiveness change what I bring to God about it?
phrases.prayer: Father, thank you for forgiving me in Christ. Give me compassion where I’m still hurting.

phrases.quote: just as God also forgave you in Christ.
phrases.question: What has God forgiven me for that helps me see this person with compassion?
phrases.prayer: Father, help me remember how you forgave me in Christ.

567.title: Return to the One Who Heals
567.studyConnection: After showing how his people have turned away, God calls them back. The people’s response begins in the second half of the verse.
567.verseContext: These are God’s words to his unfaithful people. His invitation to return comes with a promise to heal their unfaithfulness.

phrases.quote: Return, you faithless children.
phrases.question: Where have I wandered, and what would returning look like today?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me come back to you honestly.

phrases.quote: I will heal your unfaithfulness.
phrases.question: What keeps pulling me away that I need God’s help to change?
phrases.prayer: Lord, heal what I can’t straighten out on my own.

574.title: There Is No One Like You
574.studyConnection: Jeremiah describes idols that people carve, decorate, and carry. Then he addresses the living God directly.
574.verseContext: Jeremiah praises the Lord’s power in the middle of a warning against fearing or trusting objects people have made.

phrases.quote: Lord, there is no one like you.
phrases.question: When I feel uncertain, what do I treat as if it had the power I say belongs to God?
phrases.prayer: Lord, there is no one like you. Help me bring my fear to you before I reach for something I can control.

phrases.quote: You are great; your name is great in power.
phrases.question: What fear looks different when I remember God’s power?
phrases.prayer: Lord, you are great. Help me bring this fear to you.

581.title: Roots by the Water
581.studyConnection: Jeremiah sets reliance on human strength beside trust in the Lord. He pictures the one who trusts God as a tree rooted by water.
581.verseContext: The tree still faces heat and drought. Its roots reach a source of life deeper than the conditions around it.

phrases.quote: The person who trusts in the Lord,
phrases.question: When life feels dry, where do I go first for reassurance, and what would it look like to turn to the Lord there?
phrases.prayer: Lord, let my confidence take root in you when the circumstances around me feel dry.

phrases.quote: whose confidence indeed is the Lord, is blessed.
phrases.question: What do my first reactions under pressure show about where my confidence lies?
phrases.prayer: Lord, let my confidence take root in you.

588.title: What It Means to Know Me
588.studyConnection: God confronts King Jehoiakim for building his palace by exploiting workers. He points to Jehoiakim’s father, Josiah, who defended the poor and needy.
588.verseContext: God points to Josiah’s defense of people in need as a concrete example of what knowing him looks like.

phrases.quote: He took up the case of the poor and needy; then it went well.
phrases.question: Whose concern is easy for me to dismiss because it costs me something to pay attention?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me know you in the way I listen to and stand up for people who are easily overlooked.

phrases.quote: Is this not what it means to know me? This is the Lord’s declaration.
phrases.question: How does the way I listen to people in need reflect what I know of God?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help knowing you change whose concerns I take seriously.

595.title: Everlasting Love
595.studyConnection: In the midst of promises to restore Israel, God speaks of the faithful love with which he has continued to hold his people.
595.verseContext: God is speaking to Israel. His lasting love is the reason he continues to show them faithfulness and promises to rebuild them.

phrases.quote: I have loved you with an everlasting love;
phrases.question: What part of God’s faithfulness is hardest for me to remember when restoration feels slow?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me remember how faithfully you have loved your people. Give me patience to trust you while I wait.

phrases.quote: therefore, I have continued to extend faithful love to you.
phrases.question: What part of God’s faithful love is hard to remember while I wait?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me remember your faithfulness in this slow season.

602.title: Ready to Hear the Answer
602.studyConnection: After Jerusalem falls, the survivors ask Jeremiah to seek God’s direction. They pledge to obey, then reject his answer and go to Egypt.
602.verseContext: The survivors make this promise to Jeremiah. Their later refusal asks us to examine how open we really are to God’s answer.

phrases.quote: We will certainly obey the Lord our God!
phrases.question: When I ask God for guidance, what answer would I be most tempted to explain away?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me hear you honestly. Give me the willingness to obey when your answer cuts across my plans.

609.title: When Plans Grow Smaller
609.studyConnection: Baruch, Jeremiah’s scribe, is worn out by sorrow. God speaks to him while Judah is facing judgment and promises to preserve his life wherever he goes.
609.verseContext: God addresses Baruch’s pursuit of great things for himself in the middle of Judah’s collapse. His words come with a promise to preserve Baruch’s life.

phrases.quote: But as for you, do you pursue great things for yourself?
phrases.question: What ambition am I still insisting on, and what is hard about bringing it honestly before God?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me loosen my grip on what I thought my life had to become. Show me how to be faithful where I am.

phrases.quote: Stop pursuing!
phrases.question: What would it mean to loosen my grip on one ambition today?
phrases.prayer: Lord, show me what I can release and how to be faithful here.

616.title: Make Room for Their Interests
616.studyConnection: Paul urges the Philippian church toward unity and humility, then points to Jesus, who took the form of a servant.
616.verseContext: Paul asks believers to look out for one another and shows them what that humility looks like in Jesus.

phrases.quote: Everyone should look not to his own interests,
phrases.question: In a decision I’m facing, whose needs would I notice if I slowed down before defending my preference?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me see what matters to the other person and give it real weight.

phrases.quote: but rather to the interests of others.
phrases.question: Whose interests have I left out of a decision I’m making?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me notice what matters to them and give it weight.

623.title: Take It to Heart
623.studyConnection: God gives Ezekiel a scroll to eat before sending him to speak to the exiles. Ezekiel has to receive God’s words himself before carrying them to others.
623.verseContext: God tells Ezekiel to listen and take his words to heart before speaking them to the exiles, whether they listen or refuse.

phrases.quote: Son of man, listen carefully to all my words that I speak to you
phrases.question: What word from Scripture am I quick to pass along but slow to let settle into my own life?
phrases.prayer: Lord, let your words sink in before I rush to speak. Show me what it means to take them to heart today.

phrases.quote: and take them to heart.
phrases.question: What Scripture am I familiar with but slow to live by?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help your words settle into the way I live.

630.title: A Heart That Can Respond
630.studyConnection: God speaks through Ezekiel about the scattered people of Israel. He promises to gather them, renew their hearts, and enable them to walk in his ways.
630.verseContext: God promises the scattered people of Israel a change they cannot produce for themselves. Verse 20 shows what the renewed heart is for: a life of obedience with God.

phrases.quote: I will remove their heart of stone from their bodies
phrases.question: Where have I grown so used to resisting God that I scarcely notice it anymore?
phrases.prayer: Lord, soften what has grown hard in me. Help me respond when you show me the way to walk.

phrases.quote: and give them a heart of flesh,
phrases.question: What would a heart ready to respond to God look like in this situation?
phrases.prayer: Lord, make my heart willing to respond to you.

637.title: Turn and Live
637.studyConnection: God answers Israel’s complaint that his way is unfair. He holds each person responsible and calls them to turn from rebellion.
637.verseContext: God tells Israel that he takes no pleasure in anyone’s death. That is why his warning ends with an invitation to turn and live.

phrases.quote: For I take no pleasure in anyone’s death.
phrases.question: What does God’s heart here show me about why he calls people to turn?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me hear your heart behind the warning.

phrases.quote: So repent and live!
phrases.question: What is one way I could turn toward God where I’ve been resisting him?
phrases.prayer: Lord, give me the willingness to turn and receive the life you offer.

644.title: When a Gift Goes to My Head
644.studyConnection: Ezekiel’s lament addresses the king of Tyre. It describes how beauty and splendor fed pride and corrupted his wisdom.
644.verseContext: God’s lament over the king of Tyre ties the king’s pride and corrupted wisdom to the splendor he was given.

phrases.quote: Your heart became proud because of your beauty;
phrases.question: What ability or success makes me less willing to listen when someone sees something I’ve missed?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me receive the good you’ve given me with gratitude. Keep me willing to listen and learn.

phrases.quote: For the sake of your splendor you corrupted your wisdom.
phrases.question: When has wanting to look impressive made it harder to listen?
phrases.prayer: Lord, make me willing to learn even when it costs me pride.

651.title: A Shepherd Who Gives Rest
651.studyConnection: Israel’s leaders used the flock to feed themselves. God says he will gather and tend the sheep they neglected.
651.verseContext: God promises to shepherd his scattered people himself. He gives the flock the care and rest their leaders failed to provide.

phrases.quote: I will tend my flock
phrases.question: Where is it hard to believe God sees what I need?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me trust your care.

phrases.quote: and let them lie down.
phrases.question: Where am I finding it difficult to rest?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me receive the rest you give.

658.title: When Hope Has Dried Up
658.studyConnection: God tells Ezekiel that the dry bones represent the whole house of Israel, who feel cut off and say their hope is gone.
658.verseContext: The promise is to Israel in exile. God says he will put his Spirit in them, give them life, and settle them in their own land.

phrases.quote: I will put my Spirit in you, and you will live,
phrases.question: What has disappointment made me assume about God’s ability to give life where hope feels gone?
phrases.prayer: Lord, you heard your people when they said their hope was gone. Meet me where I’ve run out of hope and help me trust you there.

phrases.quote: and I will settle you in your own land.
phrases.question: What does God’s promise to restore Israel show me about his care for people who feel cut off?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me remember you heard your people when they felt cut off.

665.title: Keep Walking in Christ
665.studyConnection: Paul urges the Colossian church to continue in the Christ they received as Lord.
665.verseContext: Verse 7 describes that walk as being rooted and built up in Christ, established in the faith, and overflowing with gratitude.

phrases.quote: So then, just as you have received Christ Jesus as Lord,
phrases.question: Where am I treating something else as the thing I need most in order to grow?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me keep walking with you where I’m tempted to look elsewhere.

phrases.quote: continue to walk in him,
phrases.question: Where would continuing to walk with Jesus change what I do today?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me keep walking with you in this part of my life.

672.title: Who Holds the Seasons
672.studyConnection: Daniel and his friends ask God for mercy when the king threatens the wise men of Babylon. Daniel praises God when the mystery is revealed.
672.verseContext: Daniel says this while serving under a foreign king. He remembers that wisdom and power belong to God.

phrases.quote: He changes the times and seasons;
phrases.question: When a decision is in someone else’s hands, what helps me remember that their authority has limits?
phrases.prayer: God, you hold what I can’t control. Give me wisdom to be faithful with what’s in my hands.

phrases.quote: he removes kings and establishes kings.
phrases.question: What decision reminds me that human authority has limits?
phrases.prayer: God, help me trust you when someone else holds the decision.

679.title: Based on Your Compassion
679.studyConnection: Daniel confesses his people’s sin and pleads for Jerusalem and the sanctuary.
679.verseContext: Daniel includes himself in Israel’s confession and asks God to hear them because God is compassionate.

phrases.quote: For we are not presenting our petitions before you based on our righteous acts,
phrases.question: What have I hesitated to ask God for because I feel I haven’t earned the right to ask?
phrases.prayer: God, I come to you because you are compassionate. Help me tell you honestly what I need.

phrases.quote: but based on your abundant compassion.
phrases.question: What would I ask honestly if I trusted God’s compassion?
phrases.prayer: God, help me come to you because you are compassionate.

686.title: What Counts as Gain
686.studyConnection: Paul warns Timothy about people who treat godliness as a way to make money.
686.verseContext: Paul calls godliness with contentment great gain in a passage warning against the desire to get rich.

phrases.quote: But godliness with contentment is great gain.
phrases.question: What do I keep telling myself I need before I can be content with what God has given me today?
phrases.prayer: Father, teach me to receive what I have with gratitude. Help me see what’s worth pursuing.

693.title: Love That Stays
693.studyConnection: God asks Ephraim and Judah what to do with them because their love disappears as quickly as morning mist.
693.verseContext: God speaks to Ephraim and Judah. He wants the faithful love and knowledge of him that their offerings alone cannot express.

phrases.quote: For I desire faithful love and not sacrifice,
phrases.question: What devotion comes easily to me in the moment, and where does God invite me to keep showing up in faithful love after that moment passes?
phrases.prayer: Lord, teach me to know you and to stay faithful when the feeling fades.

phrases.quote: the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
phrases.question: Where has a familiar act of worship stopped helping me pay attention to God?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me know you in what I do today.

700.title: Loved Freely
700.studyConnection: Hosea calls Israel to return with words of repentance and to let go of the things they relied on for rescue. God responds with a promise of healing.
700.verseContext: God promises to heal Israel’s turning away and to love them freely. The promise answers the call to return in the preceding verses.

phrases.quote: I will heal their apostasy;
phrases.question: What keeps pulling me away that I need God to heal?
phrases.prayer: Lord, heal what keeps turning away from you.

phrases.quote: I will freely love them, for my anger will have turned from him.
phrases.question: Where do I still feel I have to make up for my failure before returning to God?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me come back and receive the love you give freely.

707.title: Courage to Speak of Jesus
707.studyConnection: Paul writes as a prisoner and urges Timothy to rekindle his gift and share in suffering for the gospel.
707.verseContext: Paul pairs courage with love and sound judgment as he urges Timothy to speak of Jesus even when it costs him.

phrases.quote: For God has not given us a spirit of fear,
phrases.question: Where am I afraid to speak about Jesus?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me bring my fear to you.

phrases.quote: but one of power, love, and sound judgment.
phrases.question: How could love and sound judgment shape what I say about Jesus?
phrases.prayer: Lord, give me courage to speak with love and good judgment.

714.title: Let Justice Flow
714.studyConnection: Amos confronts Israel for taking bribes and turning the needy away at the city gate, then speaks of God rejecting their worship gatherings.
714.verseContext: God calls for justice and righteousness in the same community that keeps holding feasts and singing songs while denying people a fair hearing.

phrases.quote: But let justice flow like water,
phrases.question: Who might struggle to get a fair hearing in a decision I help make?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me listen to someone others overlook.

phrases.quote: and righteousness, like an unfailing stream.
phrases.question: Where would doing what’s right require steady attention from me this week?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me keep doing what is right after the first effort.

721.title: Come for Mercy
721.studyConnection: Hebrews identifies Jesus as the great high priest who understands our weaknesses and invites believers to come to God for help.
721.verseContext: Jesus understands our weaknesses. That is why we can approach God with confidence.

phrases.quote: let us approach the throne of grace with boldness,
phrases.question: What need am I reluctant to bring to God?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me bring you what I need.

phrases.quote: so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in time of need.
phrases.question: Where do I need mercy or help today?
phrases.prayer: Father, give me mercy and the help I need today.

728.title: Hold On to Hope
728.studyConnection: After explaining the way Jesus opened through his sacrifice, the writer urges believers to draw near to God and encourage one another.
728.verseContext: The writer calls the church to hold on to hope because God, who made the promise, is faithful.

phrases.quote: Let us hold on to the confession of our hope without wavering,
phrases.question: What hope in Christ is hardest to say out loud right now?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me hold on to the hope I confess.

phrases.quote: since he who promised is faithful.
phrases.question: What changes when I think about the one who made the promise?
phrases.prayer: Father, help me trust your faithfulness when my confidence wavers.

735.title: Now God’s People
735.studyConnection: Peter describes believers coming to Christ, the living stone, and being built together into a spiritual house.
735.verseContext: Peter speaks to believers as a people God has gathered through his mercy.

phrases.quote: Once you were not a people, but now you are God’s people;
phrases.question: Where do I forget that belonging to God gives me people to belong with?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me receive the people you’ve gathered me with.

phrases.quote: you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy.
phrases.question: What am I still trying to prove that I could bring to God as someone who has received mercy?
phrases.prayer: Father, thank you for the mercy I could never earn.

742.title: My Prayer Came to You
742.studyConnection: Jonah prays from inside the fish and remembers what it was like to sink. He names God as the one who brought his life up from the pit.
742.verseContext: Jonah recalls his own distress after fleeing God. As his strength gives out, he remembers the Lord and prays.

phrases.quote: As my life was fading away, I remembered the Lord,
phrases.question: What do I tend to remember first when my strength runs out?
phrases.prayer: Lord, when I reach my limits, help me remember you.

phrases.quote: and my prayer came to you, to your holy temple.
phrases.question: What would I say if I trusted that my prayer reaches God even from here?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me speak to you from where I am today.

749.title: Walk Humbly
749.studyConnection: Micah describes the Lord’s case against his people. After recalling how God rescued them, the passage asks what response God requires.
749.verseContext: In response to questions about offerings, Micah names justice, faithfulness, and a humble walk with God.

phrases.quote: to act justly, to love faithfulness,
phrases.question: Where could I be fairer to someone who depends on me to keep my word?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me do what’s fair and keep my word today.

phrases.quote: and to walk humbly with your God.
phrases.question: Where am I most reluctant to admit I need God’s help?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me walk with you without pretending I can do it all myself.

756.title: Loved Like This
756.studyConnection: John tells believers to love one another and points to God sending his Son as the clearest picture of that love.
756.verseContext: John’s phrase “in this way” points back to God sending his Son for our sins.

phrases.quote: Dear friends, if God loved us in this way,
phrases.question: What does God sending his Son show me about how he loves me?
phrases.prayer: Father, help me receive the love you showed me in Jesus.

phrases.quote: we also must love one another.
phrases.question: Whose needs could I pay closer attention to because God has loved me?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me give someone the care I’ve received from you.

763.title: Yet I Will Rejoice
763.studyConnection: Habakkuk trembles as he waits for trouble to come. He pictures crops and livestock failing, yet resolves to rejoice in God.
763.verseContext: Habakkuk says “yet” after describing the loss of the food and animals his people depend on.

phrases.quote: yet I will celebrate in the Lord;
phrases.question: What good about God can I still name while I wait on something hard?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me remember your goodness while I wait.

phrases.quote: I will rejoice in the God of my salvation!
phrases.question: When a source of security fails, what helps me remember who can save me?
phrases.prayer: God of my salvation, help me find joy in you when I feel afraid.

770.title: God Is Among You
770.studyConnection: Zephaniah calls Jerusalem to rejoice because the Lord has removed her judgment and is among his people.
770.verseContext: The prophet speaks to Zion after judgment. God’s presence gives his people a reason to stop fearing.

phrases.quote: The Lord your God is among you,
phrases.question: When do I act as though God is far from what I’m facing?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me remember your nearness today.

phrases.quote: a warrior who saves.
phrases.question: What have I been facing as though everything depended on my strength?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me trust your strength where my own falls short.

777.title: Hold On to What You Have
777.studyConnection: Jesus speaks to the church in Philadelphia, which has little power and has kept his word.
777.verseContext: Jesus promises to come and urges a church that has already endured to keep holding on.

phrases.quote: I am coming soon.
phrases.question: How might expecting Jesus to return change what gets my attention today?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me live today expecting you.

phrases.quote: Hold on to what you have, so that no one takes your crown.
phrases.question: Where is it hardest to keep doing what I know is faithful?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me hold on to your word there.

784.title: Faith That Endures
784.studyConnection: Revelation calls believers to remain faithful to Jesus amid pressure to worship the beast.
784.verseContext: The passage describes endurance in concrete terms: keeping God’s commands and continuing to trust Jesus.

phrases.quote: This calls for endurance from the saints,
phrases.question: Where am I tired of making the same faithful choice?
phrases.prayer: Lord, give me endurance for what I face today.

phrases.quote: who keep God’s commands and their faith in Jesus.
phrases.question: What would staying faithful to Jesus look like in one decision I’m facing?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me trust you enough to obey you there.

791.title: The Beginning and the End
791.studyConnection: Near the close of Revelation, Jesus says he is coming and identifies himself as the first and the last.
791.verseContext: These are Jesus’ words about who he is as he promises to come.

phrases.quote: I am the Alpha and the Omega,
phrases.question: What am I trying to understand entirely on my own when I could bring it to Jesus?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me bring you what I can’t see clearly.

phrases.quote: the first and the last, the beginning and the end.
phrases.question: What ending am I afraid to entrust to Jesus?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me trust you with how this ends.

798.title: By My Spirit
798.studyConnection: God speaks to Zerubbabel about rebuilding the temple and promises that the hands that laid its foundation will finish it.
798.verseContext: God tells Zerubbabel where the strength to finish the temple will come from.

phrases.quote: Not by strength or by might,
phrases.question: Where am I acting as though the outcome depends entirely on me?
phrases.prayer: Lord, show me where I’m relying only on my own strength.

phrases.quote: but by my Spirit,
phrases.question: What task in front of me could I begin by asking for God’s help?
phrases.prayer: Lord, help me do my part in dependence on your Spirit.

805.title: Your King Is Coming
805.studyConnection: Zechariah calls Jerusalem to rejoice at the arrival of her king. The next verse describes him ending war and speaking peace to the nations.
805.verseContext: Zion’s king comes righteous and victorious, yet rides a donkey. Matthew 21:1–11 connects this image to Jesus’ entry into Jerusalem.

phrases.quote: Look, your King is coming to you; he is righteous and victorious,
phrases.question: Where do I need to remember that Jesus is King before I decide how to respond?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, help me make room for your rule in how I respond today.

phrases.quote: humble and riding on a donkey,
phrases.question: Where am I tempted to insist on being noticed when I could follow Jesus’ example of humility?
phrases.prayer: Jesus, teach me to follow you without needing to draw attention to myself.

812.title: The Lord Took Notice
812.studyConnection: Some of Malachi’s hearers say that serving God is useless. Others who honor him speak with one another, and the Lord listens.
812.verseContext: The Lord notices those who honor him even when people around them question whether serving him matters.

phrases.quote: The Lord took notice and listened.
phrases.question: What quiet act of faithfulness feels unseen, and how does it change things to remember that God takes notice?
phrases.prayer: Lord, thank you for noticing what others may never see. Help me stay faithful to you.
